items.readback: The real Hermitian spectral measure is the finite weighted eigenvalue measure; integrating any scalar function is its CFC quadratic form, with polynomial and moment specializations.

statement_evidence.source_signature:
theorem integral_integral_spectralMeasure_eq_trace {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
    {μ : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian)
    (f : ℝ → ℝ) {z : Ω → n → ℝ} (hz : ∀ i, MemLp (fun ω => z ω i) 2 μ)
    (hind : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → IndepFun (fun ω => z ω i) (fun ω => z ω j) μ)
    (hmean : ∀ i, ∫ ω, z ω i ∂μ = 0) (hsq : ∀ i, ∫ ω, z ω i ^ 2 ∂μ = 1) :
    ∫ ω, (∫ x, f x ∂spectralMeasure hA (z ω)) ∂μ = (cfc f A).trace
def spectralMeasure {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (v : n → ℝ) : Measure ℝ

theorem integral_spectralMeasure {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (v : n → ℝ)
    (f : ℝ → ℝ) : ∫ x, f x ∂spectralMeasure hA v = v ⬝ᵥ (cfc f A *ᵥ v)

theorem integral_eval_spectralMeasure {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (v : n → ℝ)
    (p : Polynomial ℝ) :
    ∫ x, p.eval x ∂spectralMeasure hA v = v ⬝ᵥ (Polynomial.aeval A p *ᵥ v)

theorem integral_pow_spectralMeasure {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (v : n → ℝ)
    (k : ℕ) : ∫ x, x ^ k ∂spectralMeasure hA v = v ⬝ᵥ ((A ^ k) *ᵥ v)

items.readback: An isometry containing K_q reproduces scalar polynomial quadratic forms for degree below 2q; uniform polynomial approximation gives the twice-error quadrature bound.

statement_evidence.source_signature:
theorem dotProduct_aeval_mulVec_eq (D : LanczosDecomp A b q) (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hq : 0 < q)
    {p : Polynomial ℝ} (hp : p.degree < 2 * q) :
    b ⬝ᵥ (Polynomial.aeval A p *ᵥ b) =
      (b ⬝ᵥ b) * Polynomial.aeval D.T p ⟨0, hq⟩ ⟨0, hq⟩

theorem dotProduct_cfc_T_mulVec_eq_sum (D : LanczosDecomp A b q) (hA : A.IsHermitian)
    (hq : 0 < q) (f : ℝ → ℝ) :
    (D.Qᵀ *ᵥ b) ⬝ᵥ (cfc f D.T *ᵥ (D.Qᵀ *ᵥ b)) = (b ⬝ᵥ b) * ∑ i,
      f ((D.isHermitian_T hA).eigenvalues i) *
        ((D.isHermitian_T hA).eigenvectorBasis i ⟨0, hq⟩) ^ 2

theorem dotProduct_aeval_mulVec_eq_sum (D : LanczosDecomp A b q) (hA : A.IsHermitian)
    (hq : 0 < q) {p : ℝ[X]} (hp : p.degree < 2 * q) :
    b ⬝ᵥ (aeval A p *ᵥ b) = (b ⬝ᵥ b) * ∑ i,
      p.eval ((D.isHermitian_T hA).eigenvalues i) *
        ((D.isHermitian_T hA).eigenvectorBasis i ⟨0, hq⟩) ^ 2

baseline_audit.readback: An isometry containing K_q reproduces scalar polynomial quadratic forms for degree below 2q; uniform polynomial approximation gives the twice-error quadrature bound.

statement_evidence.signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_aeval_mulVec_eq_of_degree_lt_two_mul.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {k : Type u_2} [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {Q : Matrix n k ℝ}
  (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) (b : n → ℝ) {q : ℕ} (hK : NLAlib.krylovSpace A b q ≤ Q.mulVecLin.range)
  {p : Polynomial ℝ} (hp : p.degree < 2 * ↑q) :
  b ⬝ᵥ ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec b =
    Q.transpose.mulVec b ⬝ᵥ ((Polynomial.aeval (Q.transpose * A * Q)) p).mulVec (Q.transpose.mulVec b)

NLAlib.abs_dotProduct_cfc_mulVec_sub_le_of_degree_lt_two_mul.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {k : Type u_2} [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {Q : Matrix n k ℝ}
  (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) (b : n → ℝ) {q : ℕ} (hK : NLAlib.krylovSpace A b q ≤ Q.mulVecLin.range) {f : ℝ → ℝ}
  {p : Polynomial ℝ} (hp : p.degree < 2 * ↑q) {a c E : ℝ} (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ Set.Icc a c)
  (hfp : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc a c, |f x - Polynomial.eval x p| ≤ E) :
  |b ⬝ᵥ (cfc f A).mulVec b - Q.transpose.mulVec b ⬝ᵥ (cfc f (Q.transpose * A * Q)).mulVec (Q.transpose.mulVec b)| ≤
    2 * E * ‖WithLp.toLp 2 b‖ ^ 2

NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.dotProduct_cfc_T_mulVec_eq_sum.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  {b : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} (D : NLAlib.LanczosDecomp A b q) (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hq : 0 < q) (f : ℝ → ℝ) :
  D.Q.transpose.mulVec b ⬝ᵥ (cfc f D.T).mulVec (D.Q.transpose.mulVec b) =
    b ⬝ᵥ b * ∑ i, f (⋯.eigenvalues i) * (⋯.eigenvectorBasis i).ofLp ⟨0, hq⟩ ^ 2

    (T ℝ q).eval x = ((x + √(x ^ 2 - 1)) ^ q + (x - √(x ^ 2 - 1)) ^ q) / 2

    (x + √(x ^ 2 - 1)) ^ q / 2 ≤ (T ℝ q).eval x

    minimaxError n (f.comp ⟨h, h.continuous⟩) = minimaxError n f

    (f : C(Set.Icc a b, ℝ)) :
    minimaxError n
      (f.comp ⟨((iccHomeoI (-1 : ℝ) 1 (by norm_num)).trans
        (iccHomeoI a b hab).symm), Homeomorph.continuous _⟩) = minimaxError n f

    minimaxError n f ≤ ‖f‖

theorem bernsteinIntervalLower_pos {a b ρ : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a < b)
    (hρ : 1 < ρ) (hr : ρ < (√b + √a) / (√b - √a)) :
    0 < bernsteinIntervalLower a b ρ

theorem exists_degree_le_abs_sub_eval_le_of_rightHalfPlane
    {a b ρ M : ℝ} {f : ℝ → ℝ} {F : ℂ → ℂ}
    (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a < b) (hρ : 1 < ρ)
    (hr : ρ < (√b + √a) / (√b - √a))
    (hF : DifferentiableOn ℂ F {z : ℂ | 0 < z.re})
    (hM : ∀ z : ℂ, bernsteinIntervalLower a b ρ ≤ z.re →
      ‖z‖ ≤ bernsteinIntervalUpper a b ρ → ‖F z‖ ≤ M)
    (hmatch : ∀ x ∈ Icc a b, F x = (f x : ℂ)) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ p : ℝ[X], p.degree ≤ n ∧ ∀ x ∈ Icc a b,
      |f x - p.eval x| ≤ 2 * M / ρ ^ n / (ρ - 1)

theorem exists_degree_le_abs_rpow_sub_eval_le {a b ρ : ℝ}
    (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a < b) (hρ : 1 < ρ)
    (hr : ρ < (√b + √a) / (√b - √a)) (α : ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ p : ℝ[X], p.degree ≤ n ∧ ∀ x ∈ Icc a b,
      |x ^ α - p.eval x| ≤
        2 * max ((bernsteinIntervalLower a b ρ) ^ α)
          ((bernsteinIntervalUpper a b ρ) ^ α) / ρ ^ n / (ρ - 1)

theorem exists_degree_le_abs_log_sub_eval_le {a b ρ : ℝ}
    (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a < b) (hρ : 1 < ρ)
    (hr : ρ < (√b + √a) / (√b - √a)) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ p : ℝ[X], p.degree ≤ n ∧ ∀ x ∈ Icc a b,
      |Real.log x - p.eval x| ≤
        2 * (max |Real.log (bernsteinIntervalLower a b ρ)|
          |Real.log (bernsteinIntervalUpper a b ρ)| + Real.pi / 2) / ρ ^ n / (ρ - 1)

theorem exists_sign_polynomial_of_bernstein_radius {γ ρ : ℝ} (hγ : 0 < γ)
    (hγone : γ < 1) (hρ : 1 < ρ) (hr : ρ < (1 + γ) / (1 - γ)) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ q : ℝ[X], q.degree ≤ n ∧
      (X * q.comp (X ^ 2)).degree ≤ ((2 * n + 1 : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ) ∧
      ∀ x : ℝ, γ ≤ |x| → |x| ≤ 1 →
        |Real.sign x - (X * q.comp (X ^ 2)).eval x| ≤
          2 * (bernsteinIntervalLower (γ ^ 2) 1 ρ) ^ (-(1 / 2 : ℝ)) / ρ ^ n / (ρ - 1)

theorem exists_sign_polynomial_abs_sub_eval_le {γ : ℝ} (hγ : 0 < γ)
    (hγone : γ < 1) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ q : ℝ[X], q.degree ≤ n ∧
      (X * q.comp (X ^ 2)).degree ≤ ((2 * n + 1 : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ) ∧
      ∀ x : ℝ, γ ≤ |x| → |x| ≤ 1 →
        |Real.sign x - (X * q.comp (X ^ 2)).eval x| ≤
          (4 / (√3 * γ ^ 2)) / (1 + γ) ^ n

items.readback: Actual Lanczos columns are exact-degree polynomial evaluations, orthonormal for the spectral measure; the interior three-term recurrence and monic compressed characteristic-polynomial orthogonality are proved.

statement_evidence.source_signature:
theorem integral_poly_mul_poly (D : LanczosDecomp A b q) (hA : A.IsHermitian) {i j : ℕ}
    (hi : i < q) :
    ∫ x, (D.poly i).eval x * (D.poly j).eval x ∂spectralMeasure hA b =
      if i = j then 1 else 0

theorem X_mul_poly (D : LanczosDecomp A b q) (hA : A.IsHermitian) {j : ℕ} (hj : j + 1 < q) :
    X * D.poly j = C (D.beta j) * D.poly (j - 1) + C (D.alpha j) * D.poly j +
      C (D.beta (j + 1)) * D.poly (j + 1)

theorem integral_eval_charpoly_mul_eq_zero (D : LanczosDecomp A b q) (hA : A.IsHermitian)
    {r : ℝ[X]} (hr : r.degree < q) :
    ∫ x, D.T.charpoly.eval x * r.eval x ∂spectralMeasure hA b = 0

theorem charpoly_restrict_T_mul_poly_zero (D : LanczosDecomp A b q) (hA : A.IsHermitian) {j : ℕ}
    (hj : j < q) :
    (LanczosDecomp.T (D.restrict hj.le)).charpoly * D.poly 0 =
      C (∏ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 j, D.beta k) * D.poly j

items.readback: For q≥1, squared first eigenvector coordinates are positive Gauss weights for μ_b/M, with M=‖b‖²; multiplication by M gives the original-measure rule and finite second-kind approximant. Consecutive valid leading compressions strictly interlace in descending order θ_i(T_(q+1))>θ_i(T_q)>θ_(i+1)(T_(q+1)), requiring q+1≤grade. Signed normalized CD uses 1≤m<q. A monic norm-divided kernel permits a zero-norm top polynomial when preceding norms are positive. Actual characteristic continuants and off-spectrum complex resolvents are proved. Ordinary nested fractions require every intermediate denominator nonzero, derived for nonreal shifts and the existing real-above-spectrum branch.

findings: Squared first coordinates are weights for μ_b/‖b‖². Weights for μ_b are ‖b‖² times those squares.
Strict interlacing and complex resolvent arguments are not consequences of the current non-strict and real-above-spectrum declarations.
The divided Christoffel–Darboux expression requires x≠y; at x=y use a confluent identity.

items.exact_scope: The finite unscaled resolvent is the normalized-measure approximant, not the full nonterminal Stieltjes transform. An ordinary resolvent requires the final shift off the spectrum. The totalized Cramer identity also holds at spectral poles but is not an analytic resolvent there. Real intermediate tail poles are handled by the final pole-free determinant quotient. Fully normalized top kernels require a positive top norm; divided CD requires x≠y. Order zero has scalar fraction zero and empty determinant one, without a first coordinate or normalized zero-mass measure.

reviewed_clauses.statement: The actual canonical moment Jacobi compression has monic alpha diagonal and positive square-root monic-beta adjacent entries, and its normalized polynomials satisfy the corresponding three-term recurrence. Actual signed Lanczos T has its own diagonal and signed off-diagonal coefficient matrix.

At q≥1 and mass M=‖b‖²>0, first eigenvector-coordinate squares are positive normalized μ_b/M Gauss weights; multiplication by M restores original-measure exactness through degree 2q−1. Actual Lanczos polynomials themselves remain orthonormal for μ_b.
A valid size-(q+1) decomposition requires q+1≤grade; its descending spectra satisfy θ_i(T_(q+1))>θ_i(T_q)>θ_(i+1)(T_(q+1)). The larger order may equal the grade.

Actual signed normalized multiplied/confluent CD uses 1≤m<q. Monic norm-divided kernels need preceding positive norms and allow a zero-norm top polynomial; fully normalized top kernels additionally need h_m>0.

The actual nonreal Jacobi resolvent is the literal nested complex fraction for arbitrary signed real coefficients, and every intermediate scalar Schur denominator is proved nonzero. The actual signed Lanczos matrix inherits this formula.

The totalized Cramer determinant quotient holds at every shift; an ordinary analytic resolvent requires a nonzero final determinant. It handles real intermediate tail poles off the final spectrum, and continuants equal every leading characteristic polynomial.

Original mass times the actual finite canonical Jacobi resolvent equals the second-kind ratio and original Gauss partial fraction off the actual nodes; rooted moments match through degree 2n−1, including termination. The unscaled resolvent is the normalized-measure approximant, not the full nonterminal transform.
At order zero the scalar approximant is zero and the empty characteristic denominator is one; no nonexistent first coordinate is used.

hypotheses: $A$ is real symmetric, $b\ne0$, $1\le q\le\operatorname{grade}(A,b)$, and $T_q$ is the actual compression of a graded Lanczos basis. The spectral measure $\mu_b$ has original mass $M=\|b\|^2$; squared first eigenvector coordinates integrate $\mu_b/M$.

Strict interlacing compares a size-$(q+1)$ decomposition with its leading size-$q$ restriction, so $q+1\le\operatorname{grade}(A,b)$ is required. The larger order may equal the grade; eigenvalues above are ordered nonincreasingly.

The normalized Christoffel–Darboux formula from a size-$q$ decomposition uses $1\le m<q$. A fully normalized top polynomial requires $h_m>0$; the monic norm-divided terminal formula requires only the preceding norms $h_0,\ldots,h_{m-1}>0$.

The ordinary complex resolvent and determinant quotient require $z\notin\operatorname{spec}(T_q)$. Literal nested division additionally requires every trailing-block determinant to be nonzero; this is derived for nonreal $z$ and for real $z$ above the spectrum. The divided kernel requires $x\ne y$; multiplied and confluent formulas cover the other cases.
Zero order is handled by the empty determinant and zero scalar fraction, with no first coordinate or normalized zero-mass measure.
items.conclusion: The actual Jacobi/Lanczos matrix gives simple Gauss nodes and positive normalized weights, original-mass quadrature exactness, strict consecutive interlacing, finite complex resolvent and continued-fraction identities, and multiplied/divided/confluent Christoffel–Darboux identities on their stated finite-order domains.

reviewed_clauses.statement: The squared bilinear norm of any finite monomial expansion is exactly its Hankel coefficient quadratic form.
Positive-measure Hankel matrices are positive semidefinite; positive definiteness is equivalent to the support threshold and positivity of all leading Hankel determinants, including order zero.
The canonical monic polynomial is the normalized bordered Hankel determinant, and its next coefficient is the explicitly indexed shifted Hankel determinant ratio.
Finite Hankel determinants are products of the monic norms, and norm and recurrence coefficients obey the norm, beta, and shifted alpha determinant ratios whenever their denominators are nonzero.
For the actual spectral measure the Hankel matrix is the Krylov Gram matrix and it is positive definite exactly up to the Krylov grade.

items.readback: Canonical monic measure polynomials are characteristic polynomials of their moment Jacobi matrices. Every valid actual Lanczos decomposition has the matrix derivative remainder with the squared Euclidean norm of its monic characteristic polynomial applied to the starting vector, including exact Krylov termination.

baseline_audit.readback: No Radau/Lobatto bordering, exactness or derivative-remainder theorem is present. The derivative-bound orientation is reversed; the corner formula is correct for monic det(tI−T).
findings: State χ_j(t)=det(tI−T_j) explicitly. Under this monic convention the advertised minus-sign Radau corner is correct; reversing determinant orientation changes that sign.
For a positive odd derivative the left-endpoint error integral is nonnegative, so left Radau is a lower bound and right Radau an upper bound. The card conclusion reverses these signs.
A (q+2)-node Lobatto rule is exact to degree 2q+1, but its derivative remainder order is 2q+2; terminal and endpoint support degeneracies need explicit handling.
remaining: Corrected bordered constructions, endpoint weighted-measure polynomial exactness and derivative remainders.

items.exact_scope: Exact exterior Schur-shift positivity is stated. Original support q+1 for Radau and q+2 for Lobatto are sufficient; q+1 alone is not a Lobatto positivity condition. The corner convention is chi_j(t)=det(tI-T_j), and mass weights are for the original measure.

reviewed_clauses.statement: Actual intrinsic interpolatory endpoint rules follow from modified nodal orthogonality, with degree thresholds 2q and 2q+1; weighted squared cardinal tests prove the positive weights under the original support nondegeneracy.

The actual Radau and Lobatto Schur borders have the designated endpoint eigenvalues and interval matrix order. The exact strict shift hypotheses are explicit; original support q+1 and q+2 respectively are clean sufficient conditions.

Last-coordinate cofactors yield the explicit monic minus-ratio Radau corners, positive Lobatto coupling and both common-corner formulas, and the actual appended-border monic characteristic recurrence.

Finite propagation of matrix powers preserves the original rooted moments through 2q for Radau and 2q+1 for Lobatto. The canonical Jacobi matrix supplies those original measure moments, including its displayed terminal order.

The constructed endpoint matrices' actual eigenvalue/first-coordinate-weight rules have the stated polynomial exactness, distinct nodes, positive weights and original total mass. Their remaining nodal products are the canonical modified monic polynomials, and these weighted functionals are native polynomial-density measure integrals.

The actual endpoint matrices have single-interior-point odd/even derivative remainders. Nonnegative odd derivatives give left Radau lower and right Radau upper bounds; nonnegative even derivatives give the Lobatto upper bound, with original operator quadratic-form consumers. Every orientation is reversed for a nonpositive derivative.

An opposite endpoint in a Radau rule forces exactness for every function, so the derivative formula retains zero signed nodal norm without requiring endpoint jets. Intrinsic zero-nodal-norm rules also cover finite atomic termination independently of smoothness. The actual canonical terminal Gauss rule supplies the finite-support fallback for any function without assuming an output exactness certificate or smoothness.

The explicit zero-order two-endpoint affine weights are nonnegative and preserve total mass without strict endpoint shifts, including a vanishing endpoint weight and the zero measure; a coincident-endpoint interval has its exact one-node mass rule.
The actual Lobatto rule reproduces every original polynomial pairing within its degree threshold, giving discrete orthogonality whenever the degree sum is at most 2q+1.
The explicit first-kind Chebyshev Lobatto cosine rule has the endpoint half weights, degree 2N-1 exactness, positivity, mass pi, and boundary/interior discrete mode norms.

reviewed_clauses.statement: The exact X-z quotient is monic of degree n and orthogonal for the weighted functional, is its canonical monic polynomial, and has modified norm equal to q_n times the original norm. Nonvanishing original evaluations make the required modified Hankel systems nonsingular; a globally quasi-definite functional remains quasi-definite under the all-order condition.

The quotient is the scaled reproducing kernel. At real modification points for a positive measure its transformed value is nonzero when the original value is nonzero; exterior real support intervals derive the original nonvanishing. No arbitrary complex transformed nonvanishing is asserted.

The original alpha coefficient equals z+q_n+e_(n-1) with zero boundary; modified alpha equals z+q_n+e_n and modified positive-order beta equals q_n e_(n-1), under only the required finite moment systems and nonvanishing evaluations. The alpha identity includes zero next norm at finite-support termination.

The actual finite monic Jacobi matrix minus zI equals its bidiagonal LU product, and the modified matrix equals the reversed product plus zI and its precise terminal-coordinate correction. Both hold under finite-prefix hypotheses and include empty and terminal atomic matrices.

The actual X-weighted spectral moment pairing is matrix A-energy; for SPD A it is nondegenerate through grade and derives zero-shift denominator nonvanishing. The actual finite spectral and energy-weighted monic Jacobi matrices have their respective forward and corrected reversed Christoffel factorization.

Before termination the actual zero-shift Christoffel Krylov vectors are nonzero graded directions and mutually A-conjugate. Every nonzero direction in the next Krylov space orthogonal in A-energy to the preceding space is their nonzero scalar multiple, establishing the mathematical CG direction interpretation up to normalization.

For an actual SPD symmetric Jacobi matrix the recursively defined LDL pivots are positive and the explicit unit lower bidiagonal LDL transpose product equals the matrix. The actual SPD Lanczos compression has the same positive-pivot factorization.

items.exact_scope: Infinite support supplies all Markov orders; finite support terminates at its exact atomic transform. Literal complex Jacobi fractions use nonreal shifts with nonzero tails; robust off-node polynomial ratios and resolvents also cover real gaps. Mass is distinct from the recurrence beta_0 boundary.

reviewed_clauses.statement: The total second-kind numerator has zero order zero, constant original mass at order one, degree at most n-1, and the monic three-term numerator recurrence.
The numerator is the actual functional polynomial divided difference and, for a positive compactly supported real measure, its actual complex Bochner divided-difference integral.
Associated monic polynomials have exactly their order as degree and obey the recurrence with an arbitrary fixed coefficient shift; the numerator is original mass times the first associated sequence.

The numerator/denominator ratio is the Gauss partial fraction over any scalar field extension; the actual canonical Gauss weights are the numerator divided by the denominator derivative at their distinct nodes.
The native Stieltjes error is exactly rho_n/pi_n and exactly the squared-monic-norm Cauchy integral divided by pi_n squared, with denominator nonvanishing proved from support exclusion.
The quantitative finite moment-matching estimate is 2 times original mass times R^(2n)/(norm(z)^(2n)*(norm(z)-R)), giving the advertised order at infinity.

For infinite compact support the actual ratios converge to the native transform uniformly on every compact complex set outside the support enclosure; at finite-support termination the ratio already equals the transform exactly.

Every actual real Hermitian matrix's scalar-extended resolvent has its spectral partial fraction at every complex point outside its actual spectrum. The actual canonical Jacobi first-coordinate resolvent gives the same second-kind ratio with the original measure mass included; away from the real axis the actual Jacobi recurrence gives its ordinary continued fraction.

items.readback: Negation-invariant moment measures have canonical polynomial parity and zero diagonals. The even and odd monic sequences equal the native square pushforwards of mu and x^2*mu composed with X^2, with the odd X factor. Actual rectangular symmetric dilations have the symmetric spectral measure and both left/right normal-matrix square pushforwards, and actual even/odd augmented Lanczos charpolys inherit these reductions through termination.

reviewed_clauses.statement: For every defined order of a symmetric positive polynomial-moment measure, the canonical monic polynomial has its degree parity and the recurrence diagonal vanishes, including support termination.

The even canonical monic polynomials are the canonical monic polynomials of the native square pushforward composed with X², and the odd canonical polynomials are X times those of the native weighted square pushforward composed with X².

The actual rectangular symmetric dilation at the upper-block seed has a native symmetric spectral measure; its square pushforward is the left normal matrix spectral measure at the original seed, and its weighted square pushforward is the right normal matrix spectral measure at the transposed seed.

Every valid actual even-order augmented Lanczos monic characteristic polynomial reduces to the left-normal canonical polynomial at X², and every odd-order one reduces to X times the right-normal canonical polynomial at X², including Krylov termination.

A size-q stored coupling a_j=D.beta j gives monic β_j=a_j² for 0<j<q, h_j=M∏a_i² for j<q, and alpha norm quotients only at positive h_j.     (L : 𝕜[X] →ₗ[𝕜] 𝕜) (n : ℕ)
    (hL : ∀ k ≤ n + 1, hankelMomentDet L k ≠ 0) :
    monicOrthogonalPolynomial L (n + 1) =
      (X - C (orthogonalRecurrenceAlpha L n)) * monicOrthogonalPolynomial L n -
        C (orthogonalRecurrenceBeta L n) * monicOrthogonalPolynomial L (n - 1)

theorem charpoly_restrict_T_succ_eq (D : LanczosDecomp A b q) (hA : A.IsHermitian)
    {j : ℕ} (hj : j + 1 ≤ q) :
    (LanczosDecomp.T (D.restrict hj)).charpoly =
      (X - C (D.alpha j)) * (LanczosDecomp.T (D.restrict (by omega : j ≤ q))).charpoly -
        C (D.beta j ^ 2) * (LanczosDecomp.T (D.restrict (by omega : j - 1 ≤ q))).charpoly

theorem orthogonalPolynomialNorm_mul_prod_beta_eq {𝕜 : Type*} [Field 𝕜]
    (L : 𝕜[X] →ₗ[𝕜] 𝕜) (n : ℕ) (hL : ∀ j ≤ n, hankelMomentDet L j ≠ 0)
    (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ n) :
    orthogonalPolynomialNorm L k *
      (∏ i ∈ Ico (k + 1) (n + 1), orthogonalRecurrenceBeta L i) =
        orthogonalPolynomialNorm L n

theorem integral_sq_charpoly_restrict_T_eq_norm_sq_mul_prod_beta_sq
    (D : LanczosDecomp A b q) (hA : A.IsHermitian) {j : ℕ} (hj : j < q) :
    (∫ x, ((LanczosDecomp.T (D.restrict hj.le)).charpoly.eval x) ^ 2 ∂spectralMeasure hA b) =
      ‖WithLp.toLp 2 b‖ ^ 2 * ∏ k ∈ Icc 1 j, D.beta k ^ 2

theorem orthogonalPolynomialJacobiMatrix_apply_self_eq_alpha (L : ℝ[X] →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ)
    {n : ℕ} (i : Fin n) (hH : 0 < orthogonalPolynomialNorm L i.val) :
    orthogonalPolynomialJacobiMatrix L n i i = orthogonalRecurrenceAlpha L i.val

theorem orthogonalPolynomialJacobiMatrix_superdiagonal_eq_sqrt_beta
    (L : ℝ[X] →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) {n : ℕ} (hL : ∀ k ≤ n, hankelMomentDet L k ≠ 0)
    (hH : ∀ k < n, 0 < orthogonalPolynomialNorm L k) (i j : Fin n)
    (hij : i.val + 1 = j.val) :
    orthogonalPolynomialJacobiMatrix L n i j = Real.sqrt (orthogonalRecurrenceBeta L j.val)

theorem sq_orthogonalPolynomialJacobiMatrix_superdiagonal_eq_beta
    (L : ℝ[X] →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) {n : ℕ} (hL : ∀ k ≤ n, hankelMomentDet L k ≠ 0)
    (hH : ∀ k < n, 0 < orthogonalPolynomialNorm L k) (i j : Fin n)
    (hij : i.val + 1 = j.val) :
    orthogonalPolynomialJacobiMatrix L n i j ^ 2 = orthogonalRecurrenceBeta L j.val

theorem orthogonalRecurrenceAlpha_spectralMeasure_eq_alpha (D : LanczosDecomp A b q)
    (hA : A.IsHermitian) {j : ℕ} (hj : j < q) :
    orthogonalRecurrenceAlpha
      (polynomialIntegral (spectralMeasure hA b) (hasPolynomialMoments_spectralMeasure hA b)) j =
        D.alpha j

theorem orthogonalRecurrenceBeta_spectralMeasure_eq_beta_sq (D : LanczosDecomp A b q)
    (hA : A.IsHermitian) {j : ℕ} (hj : j < q) :
    orthogonalRecurrenceBeta
      (polynomialIntegral (spectralMeasure hA b) (hasPolynomialMoments_spectralMeasure hA b)) j =
        D.beta j ^ 2

theorem X_mul_orthonormalMomentPolynomial (L : ℝ[X] →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) (n : ℕ)
    (hL : ∀ k ≤ n + 1, hankelMomentDet L k ≠ 0)
    (hH : ∀ k ≤ n + 1, 0 < orthogonalPolynomialNorm L k) :
    X * orthonormalMomentPolynomial L n =
      C (Real.sqrt (orthogonalRecurrenceBeta L n)) * orthonormalMomentPolynomial L (n - 1) +
      C (orthogonalRecurrenceAlpha L n) * orthonormalMomentPolynomial L n +
      C (Real.sqrt (orthogonalRecurrenceBeta L (n + 1))) * orthonormalMomentPolynomial L (n + 1)

theorem orthogonalPolynomialJacobiMatrix_eq_jacobiMatrix (L : ℝ[X] →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) (n : ℕ)
    (hL : ∀ k ≤ n, hankelMomentDet L k ≠ 0)
    (hH : ∀ k < n, 0 < orthogonalPolynomialNorm L k) :
    orthogonalPolynomialJacobiMatrix L n =
      jacobiMatrix (orthogonalRecurrenceAlpha L) (fun i => Real.sqrt (orthogonalRecurrenceBeta L i)) n

theorem sub_mul_sum_prod_beta_mul_eval_monicOrthogonalPolynomial {𝕜 : Type*} [Field 𝕜]
    (L : 𝕜[X] →ₗ[𝕜] 𝕜) (n : ℕ) (hL : ∀ j ≤ n + 1, hankelMomentDet L j ≠ 0)
    (x y : 𝕜) :
    (x - y) * (∑ k ∈ range (n + 1),
      (∏ i ∈ Ico (k + 1) (n + 1), orthogonalRecurrenceBeta L i) *
        (monicOrthogonalPolynomial L k).eval x * (monicOrthogonalPolynomial L k).eval y) =
      (monicOrthogonalPolynomial L (n + 1)).eval x * (monicOrthogonalPolynomial L n).eval y -
        (monicOrthogonalPolynomial L n).eval x * (monicOrthogonalPolynomial L (n + 1)).eval y

theorem sum_sq_eval_orthonormalMomentPolynomial_eq_confluent_and_pos
    (L : ℝ[X] →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) (n : ℕ) (hL : ∀ j ≤ n + 1, hankelMomentDet L j ≠ 0)
    (hH : ∀ j ≤ n, 0 < orthogonalPolynomialNorm L j) (x : ℝ) :
    (∑ k ∈ range (n + 1), (orthonormalMomentPolynomial L k).eval x ^ 2) =
      ((monicOrthogonalPolynomial L (n + 1)).derivative.eval x *
        (monicOrthogonalPolynomial L n).eval x -
        (monicOrthogonalPolynomial L n).derivative.eval x *
          (monicOrthogonalPolynomial L (n + 1)).eval x) / orthogonalPolynomialNorm L n ∧
      0 < ∑ k ∈ range (n + 1), (orthonormalMomentPolynomial L k).eval x ^ 2

theorem sum_sq_eval_orthonormalMomentPolynomial_eq_normalized_confluent_and_pos
    (L : ℝ[X] →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) (n : ℕ) (hL : ∀ j ≤ n + 1, hankelMomentDet L j ≠ 0)
    (hH : ∀ j ≤ n + 1, 0 < orthogonalPolynomialNorm L j) (x : ℝ) :
    (∑ k ∈ range (n + 1), (orthonormalMomentPolynomial L k).eval x ^ 2) =
      Real.sqrt (orthogonalRecurrenceBeta L (n + 1)) *
        ((orthonormalMomentPolynomial L (n + 1)).derivative.eval x *
          (orthonormalMomentPolynomial L n).eval x -
          (orthonormalMomentPolynomial L n).derivative.eval x *
            (orthonormalMomentPolynomial L (n + 1)).eval x) ∧
      0 < ∑ k ∈ range (n + 1), (orthonormalMomentPolynomial L k).eval x ^ 2

theorem sum_sq_eval_poly_eq_confluent_and_pos (D : LanczosDecomp A b q) (hA : A.IsHermitian)
    {m : ℕ} (hm0 : 0 < m) (hm : m < q) (x : ℝ) :
    (∑ j ∈ range m, (D.poly j).eval x ^ 2) =
      D.beta m * ((D.poly m).derivative.eval x * (D.poly (m - 1)).eval x -
        (D.poly (m - 1)).derivative.eval x * (D.poly m).eval x) ∧
      0 < ∑ j ∈ range m, (D.poly j).eval x ^ 2

theorem eval_jacobiContinuant_eq_det {𝕜 : Type*} [Field 𝕜] (a β : ℕ → 𝕜) (n : ℕ)
    (x : 𝕜) : (jacobiContinuant a β n).eval x =

theorem charpoly_jacobiMatrix_eq_jacobiContinuant {𝕜 : Type*} [Field 𝕜] [Infinite 𝕜]
    (a β : ℕ → 𝕜) (n : ℕ) : (jacobiMatrix a β n).charpoly = jacobiContinuant a β n

theorem jacobiContinuant_eq_charpoly_restrict_T (D : LanczosDecomp A b q) (hA : A.IsHermitian)
    {j : ℕ} (hj : j ≤ q) :
    jacobiContinuant D.alpha D.beta j = (LanczosDecomp.T (D.restrict hj)).charpoly

@[simp] theorem jacobiContinuant_zero {𝕜 : Type*} [Field 𝕜] (a β : ℕ → 𝕜) :
    jacobiContinuant a β 0 = 1

theorem integral_sq_charpoly_T_eq_zero_of_eq_grade (D : LanczosDecomp A b q)
    (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hq : q = krylovGrade A b) :

    (D : LanczosDecomp A b q) (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hq : q = krylovGrade A b) :
    orthogonalRecurrenceBeta

baseline_audit.readback: Canonical nonsingular moment polynomials satisfy the full monic three-term recurrence, including the zero-order boundary. The existing Lanczos API contains off-diagonal Christoffel–Darboux; the full norm-product, quotient, confluent and denominator clauses need additional bridges.
remaining: Actual signed Lanczos norm/ratio and product-weighted CD wrappers; normalized positive confluent and continued-fraction denominator B_k specialization. Generic finite monic recurrence, norm product, multiplied/confluent CD and canonical Jacobi charpoly identities are proved.

items.exact_scope: Mass h_0=M is distinct from recurrence β_0=0. Size q totalizes its absent coupling a_q to zero; it cannot compute a nonterminal h_q, which needs the next actual coupling or a larger decomposition. For diag(0,1), seed (1,1), q=1, h_1=1/2 although D.beta 1=0. No terminal zero-norm alpha quotient or normalized polynomial is asserted. Monic confluent kernels need m>0 and preceding h_0,…,h_(m−1)>0; fully normalized top kernels additionally need h_m>0. Division by x−y requires x≠y.

reviewed_clauses.statement: Canonical monic recurrences include order zero and finite-support termination; actual signed characteristic recurrences hold for j+1≤q using only the preceding stored coupling.
Generic monic products and two-order telescopes use norm-ratio beta. Actual signed size-q norm products use j<q, with every coupling 0<i≤j stored. A nonterminal h_q needs the next actual coupling.

Canonical alpha is a positive-norm quotient and positive adjacent entries are sqrt(monic beta). Actual size-q alpha quotients use j<q and monic beta equals the signed coupling square for 0<j<q. No terminal zero-norm alpha is asserted.
Positive monic norms give the normalized canonical three-term recurrence with square-root-beta coefficients. No terminal zero-norm polynomial is normalized.

The multiplied monic Christoffel–Darboux polynomial identity is valid for all x,y, and its explicit recurrence-product weighted sum has the advertised monic numerator. Division by x-y is used only when x differs from y.

The nonempty monic norm-divided confluent kernel needs m>0 and preceding positive norms, permitting a zero-norm top monic polynomial. Fully normalized Wronskians need h_m>0; actual signed normalized Wronskians use 1≤m<q.

The actual finite Jacobi denominator continuants are the monic characteristic polynomials, including the empty order-zero denominator. Every leading signed Lanczos characteristic polynomial equals its coefficient continuant; this is the advertised denominator identification, not an equivalence hypothesis.

At exact grade the actual final monic norm is zero and the final monic beta equals the squared zero terminal coupling, including the zero-grade coefficient boundary. Mass h0 remains distinct from the boundary recurrence beta0=0.

hypotheses: $A$ is real symmetric and $\mu_b=\sum_i(u_i^\top b)^2\delta_{\lambda_i}$ is its original spectral measure, of mass $\|b\|^2$. The actual Lanczos decomposition has size $q\le\operatorname{grade}(A,b)$.

Signed Lanczos couplings a_j are stored only for 0<j<q. The monic coefficient β_j is the norm ratio, equal to a_j² on these stored indices; β_0=0 is distinct from h_0. The monic alpha quotient is used only where h_j>0, in particular j<q; no terminal zero-norm alpha is asserted.

The actual characteristic recurrence includes j+1≤q, including the final polynomial, and uses only the preceding stored coupling. Norm products using size-q stored couplings require j<q. At a nonterminal top order use a larger decomposition or the next actual coupling; at exact grade the final monic norm and terminal beta are zero.

The monic multiplied Christoffel–Darboux identity holds for all x,y, with the needed finite nonsingular Hankel systems. Its divided form requires x≠y. Positive confluent kernels require m>0 and h_0,…,h_(m−1)>0 and may use a zero-norm terminal top monic polynomial. The fully normalized top-polynomial form additionally requires h_m>0; the actual signed size-q formula uses 1≤m<q.

Characteristic/continuant identification includes every leading order j≤q and does not require literal nested fraction denominators to be nonzero. Evaluating an ordinary nested fraction uses the denominator conditions of jacobi-matrix-identities.
items.conclusion: The actual leading characteristic polynomials have the monic three-term recurrence, stored-index norm products and alpha/beta norm quotients; generic finite monic norm products, terminal zero norms, monic and normalized confluent kernels, and actual continued-fraction denominator identification hold with the stated boundary conventions.

items.readback: For actual positive measures with polynomial moments, convergence of the first 2n monomial moments gives Hankel determinant convergence, including singular limiting systems and the empty determinant. With limiting support size at least n, it also gives canonical monic coefficients through n, included norms and alpha/beta below n, uniform polynomial convergence on bounded real sets, spectral-distance Jacobi convergence, and canonically ordered Gauss nodes and original-measure cardinal weights. Approximating Hankel systems are eventually positive definite; early systems may be singular.

reviewed_clauses.statement: Actual Hankel determinant convergence follows from first-2n moment convergence without limiting nondegeneracy, including the empty determinant. With limiting support at least n, the approximating positive-measure Hankel systems are eventually positive definite.

Every coefficient of each actual canonical monic measure polynomial through order n converges; every included squared norm and monic alpha/beta recurrence coefficient converges for k<n, including the constant zero beta boundary convention.
Actual measure monic polynomials through order n converge uniformly on every bounded real set and in particular the order-n polynomial converges uniformly on each fixed compact interval [a,b].
The actual normalized measure Jacobi matrices converge in spectral distance, and the actual canonically ordered n-point Gauss nodes and integrated-cardinal weights converge at each index.

hypotheses: The measures $\mu_N$ and $\mu$ are finite positive real measures with the required polynomial moments (in particular finite positive measures supported on a fixed compact interval).
For every $0\le k<2n$, the actual monomial moments $\int t^k\,d\mu_N$ converge to $\int t^k\,d\mu$.
The limiting support contains at least $n$ points. Early approximating Hankel systems may be singular; positivity is derived eventually from the limiting condition.
items.conclusion: The actual monic polynomials through degree $n$, squared norms and monic recurrence coefficients below $n$, canonically ordered $n$-point Gauss nodes, and original-measure integrated-cardinal weights converge. The polynomials converge uniformly on every bounded real set; Hankel systems are eventually positive definite and Jacobi matrices converge in spectral distance.

theorem stieltjesTransform_sub_secondKind_div_eq_integral
    {μ : Measure ℝ} (hμ : HasPolynomialMoments μ) {a b : ℝ}
    (hs : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, x ∈ Icc a b) {n : ℕ} (hn0 : 0 < n)
    (hn : (n : ℕ∞) ≤ μ.support.encard) {z : ℂ}
    (hz : ∀ x ∈ Icc a b, z ≠ (x : ℂ)) :
    stieltjesTransform μ z -
      ((secondKindPolynomial (polynomialIntegral μ hμ) n).map Complex.ofRealHom).eval z /
        ((monicOrthogonalPolynomial (polynomialIntegral μ hμ) n).map Complex.ofRealHom).eval z =
      (∫ x : ℝ, ((monicOrthogonalPolynomial (polynomialIntegral μ hμ) n).map
        Complex.ofRealHom).eval (x : ℂ) / (z - (x : ℂ)) ∂μ) /
        ((monicOrthogonalPolynomial (polynomialIntegral μ hμ) n).map Complex.ofRealHom).eval z

theorem stieltjesTransform_sub_secondKind_div_eq_integral_sq
    {μ : Measure ℝ} (hμ : HasPolynomialMoments μ) {a b : ℝ}
    (hs : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, x ∈ Icc a b) {n : ℕ} (hn0 : 0 < n)
    (hn : (n : ℕ∞) ≤ μ.support.encard) {z : ℂ}
    (hz : ∀ x ∈ Icc a b, z ≠ (x : ℂ)) :
    stieltjesTransform μ z -
      ((secondKindPolynomial (polynomialIntegral μ hμ) n).map Complex.ofRealHom).eval z /
        ((monicOrthogonalPolynomial (polynomialIntegral μ hμ) n).map Complex.ofRealHom).eval z =
      (∫ x : ℝ, ((monicOrthogonalPolynomial (polynomialIntegral μ hμ) n).map
        Complex.ofRealHom).eval (x : ℂ)^2 / (z - (x : ℂ)) ∂μ) /
        ((monicOrthogonalPolynomial (polynomialIntegral μ hμ) n).map Complex.ofRealHom).eval z^2

theorem norm_stieltjesTransform_sub_secondKind_div_le
    {μ : Measure ℝ} (hμ : HasPolynomialMoments μ) {a b : ℝ}
    (hs : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, x ∈ Icc a b) {n : ℕ} (hn0 : 0 < n)
    (hn : (n : ℕ∞) ≤ μ.support.encard) {z : ℂ} {δ : ℝ} (hδ : 0 < δ)
    (hgap : ∀ x ∈ Icc a b, δ ≤ ‖z - (x : ℂ)‖) :
    ‖stieltjesTransform μ z -
      ((secondKindPolynomial (polynomialIntegral μ hμ) n).map Complex.ofRealHom).eval z /
        ((monicOrthogonalPolynomial (polynomialIntegral μ hμ) n).map Complex.ofRealHom).eval z‖ ≤
      orthogonalPolynomialNorm (polynomialIntegral μ hμ) n /
        (δ * ‖((monicOrthogonalPolynomial (polynomialIntegral μ hμ) n).map
          Complex.ofRealHom).eval z‖^2)

    (α β c : ℕ → R) (y : ℕ → M)
    (hy : ∀ k, y (k + 2) = α (k + 1) • y (k + 1) - β (k + 1) • y k)

      (clenshawState α β c k n).2 • (y (k + 1) - α k • y k)

      (clenshawState (fun _ => 2 * t) (fun _ => 1) c 0 (n + 1)).1 -
        t * (clenshawState (fun _ => 2 * t) (fun _ => 1) c 0 (n + 1)).2

reviewed_clauses.statement: Actual degree-bounded real minimizers exist, the even-degree Chebyshev comparison gives E_(2m) <= 2/(pi*(2m+1)), and symmetrization proves E_(2m+1)=E_(2m).

For each alpha in (0,1), every positive target degree compares to every sufficiently large even source degree via the actual finite polynomial scaling and an explicit exponentially decaying target-degree remainder.
The actual scaled native minimax error n*E_n converges along all integer degrees to the real constant defined by its even-degree liminf.

The actual finite modulated Fejer dual annihilates all competitors of the prescribed degree, has uniform functional norm at most one, and yields E_n >= 1/(18*pi*(n+1)). No dual certificate is assumed as a hypothesis.
The Bernstein limit is strictly positive and lies in [1/(18*pi),2/pi]; a positive constant with the full scaled limit therefore exists.

reviewed_clauses.statement: Every polynomial degree has exact uniform best error one half for exp(-x) on the positive half-line and exp(x) on the negative half-line, expressed as the least attainable uniform bound.

The actual finite two-resolvent denominator has the displayed finite derivative formula and exact degree, and after x=4t is positive on the entire half-line with strictly positive derivative in positive degree.
The actual explicit reciprocal approximation has uniform error at most sqrt(40/21)/3^n, hence at most sqrt(2)/3^n, in every degree including degree zero.
The native canonical RatFunc type-(0,n) pole-free minimax infimum has geometric lower and upper bounds with the finite truncation prefactor; every finite degree has strictly positive error.
The actual type-(0,n) rational minimax error on the positive half-line has exact nth-root limit one third.

Affine reflection preserves the exact canonical rational error-bound set and its infimum, so the original atlas orientation exp(x) on the negative half-line has the same geometric bounds and exact nth-root limit one third.

For any finite real symmetric or complex Hermitian positive semidefinite matrix, including the empty size, the explicit denominator evaluates to a positive definite matrix and its inverse approximates the actual matrix exponential in spectral norm with the same dimension-independent scalar bound.
